newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Rebels, police killed in latest Colombia clashes.
newsitem.headline: Rebels, police killed in latest Colombia clashes.

text.p: About 150 leftist guerrillas overran a town in a remote region of western Colombia on Tuesday, killing six policemen and taking three medical workers prisoner, a police spokesman said.

He said the pre-dawn raid against the remote town of Babado in western Choco province was carried out by the National Liberation Army (ELN), a Cuban-inspired force set up by radical Roman Catholilc priests in the mid-1960s.
The rebels cut all power and phone wires before storming the town and attacking the police post. They captured a doctor and two nurses before melting back into the surrounding jungle.
In a separate clash in northern Cesar province on Tuesday, the army killed three ELN rebels near the village of Jagua de Ibirico during a routine counter-insurgency patrol, a military spokesman said.
The military on Monday said it would create new anti-guerrilla units and recruit about 3,500 new combat troops as part of an emergency defence plan to crush the rebel insurgency.

The attack on Bagado is the third major guerrilla action in Choco province in three weeks. ELN rebels attacked the town of Riosucio in the northern part of the province on Jan. 10, killing one policeman, and a week later the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) ambushed a convoy of marines, killing four and taking 10 prisoner.
